imagePrompt: Create one 1536 x 1024 pixel painted scene sheet, EXACTLY TWO COLUMNS BY THREE ROWS, six equal-width WIDE cinematic panels in row-major order 0 to 5. Each column is 768 pixels; rows are approximately 341, 341 and 342 pixels high. Hard straight cell edges; no gutters, no panel labels, no numbers, no captions, no typography, no readable lettering, no logos. Every cell is its own complete environment, never a sprite or a cutout. Use the polished watercolor and fine ink on textured cream paper style of Enough: warm directional light, deep teal and umber shadows, restrained paper grain, expressive natural faces, subtle imperfect painted edges. Human anatomy is believable, heads naturally sized; shoulders, elbows, wrists, hands, hips and knees belong to one continuous body. Seat hips on the actual seat, feet on the same floor, fingers visibly holding their actual objects; no disembodied hands, duplicated limbs, floating props or pasted-on heads. Keep important faces, hands, contact points and grounded figures within each wide panel with safe margins. Maintain the same identities, clothing, figure scale, prop design and spatial continuity across all six scenes. Anonymous original visual casting only, not likenesses of credited storytellers. This is a dramatic storyboard adaptation, not a claim that imagined symbols or staged details are verified events. Story: Everybody Had Advice. Palette accents: #E5D5E9, #566A87, #E7A97E. Identity continuity: TEEN: The same teenage boy with tan skin, short dark brown hair, muted lavender-purple shirt and slate trousers; adolescent scale, self-conscious but not childish caricature. TEACHER: The same adult woman with deeper warm brown skin, long dark brown hair, muted teal blouse and slate skirt, practical shoes; respectful rather than moralizing. FRIEND ONE: An existing offscreen teenage advice voice from one side. No new visible friend, love interest, identity or romantic outcome is invented. FRIEND TWO: A second existing offscreen teenage advice voice from the opposite side, clearly distinct from FRIEND ONE and from the teacher. TOP LEFT (frame 0): In a modest school common room, the teenager sits on a real chair under several low hovering empty advice-shapes, each a different muted contour, leaving his head and shoulders readable. His hands hold the chair edges lightly and he looks between the shapes with uncertain eyes. A second empty chair waits off to one side near a window. The symbolic shapes imply contradictory voices without any painted words, literal collision with his head or physically shrinking body. TOP RIGHT (frame 1): A large warm-colored empty speech-shape presses into the composition from the left, while the teen turns toward that offscreen friend's voice. One hand lifts half-way as if about to agree, elbow attached naturally; the other still rests on the seat. His face is startled and pulled toward somebody else's confidence. Keep the school chair, window and body scale consistent, with plenty of breathing space below the symbolic ceiling. No visible friend or romantic partner is introduced. MIDDLE LEFT (frame 2): A differently shaped cool-purple empty advice bubble pushes from the right as the left shape remains at the edge. The teen turns back the other way, raised hand now hesitating, shoulders angled between the contradictory directions. His knees and feet remain ordinary and grounded, not twisted like a puppet. The room has not changed. The two voices are separate offscreen perspectives, not a literal fight or bullying mob. MIDDLE RIGHT (frame 3): The teenager draws his shoulders in and lets both hands rest loosely near his knees, eyes lowered after the competing voices. The empty advice-shapes hang above but have stopped pressing; his body stays its real adolescent size rather than magically shrinking. The spare chair and open school window remain visible. His mouth is small and honest, admitting uncertainty without tears or humiliation. Keep attention on the person under the opinions. BOTTOM LEFT (frame 4): The teacher has brought the second chair beside and slightly facing the teen, both seats clearly supported on the same floor. She sits at a respectful distance with a small open hand over her own knee; he turns toward her, no longer gripping his seat. The advice shapes have settled into faint stationary outlines high above. Their faces meet at a natural eye line, an ordinary conversation rather than a lecture or adult looming over a child. BOTTOM RIGHT (frame 5): The symbolic ceiling has cleared. The teen sits more open toward the teacher, hands relaxed and one palm slightly turned upward as he recognizes the possibility of listening first. She attends quietly with a small encouraging expression, not a congratulatory sermon. Two chairs, a window and an unremarkable school room fill the warm wide panel. No crush, date, kiss, text-message reply or successful romantic outcome is shown; this is a respectful beginning, not a resolved romance. Story-specific safeguards: FRIEND ONE and FRIEND TWO remain offscreen and distinct. No new visible love interest, identity, date, confession result or romantic success is invented. The teacher asks about respect and the other person's wishes; do not turn the ending into a generic moral caption.
